The facts leading to pass the present award are that Police has filed a Detailed Accident Report (DAR) with respect to accident occurred on 29.12.2016.

Brief facts of the present case are that on 29.12.2016, at about 5.00 P.M, the petitioner was going from his residence at Raja Puri, New Delhi to Madhu Vihar, Dwarka, New Delhi for some work by foot on extreme left side of the road.

When he reached at Gali No.39, near ATM, Rajapuri Road, New Delhi, all of a sudden an offending vehicle bearing No.HR55X0981 being driven by its driver came in rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner from his back side.
As a result of which petitioner suffered sever injuries all over his body.

The Petitioner was taken to DDU hospital for treatment where he remained admitted wef Rakesh Kumar vs Md Naushad on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24388734/

9. PW 1 has been duly cross examined on behalf of respondent No.3.
The testimony of the PW1 with respect to negligent driving by R.1 could not be impeached.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
The evidence which has come on the file can be considered and becomes more relevant when there is no specific evidence led by other side in rebuttal.
Even otherwise strict rule that negligence is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt is not to be proved in MACT proceedings.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the file only can be considered.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that petitioner was at fault.
The charge sheet was filed against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against such implication in the present case.

So this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondents by holding that petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing No. HR55X0981 by respondent No.1 ISSUE No.2: ? Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned is entitled to compensation , if so , what amount and from whom?... OPP.
10.
Being injured, petitioner is well within his rights to claim compensation.
It is there on record that after the accident petitioner was removed to DDU Hospital where he remained admitted wef 30.12.2016 to 11.01.2017.
He was operated and got treatment of injuries received in the accident.
He has deposed that he sustained grievous injuries ie fracture of both bones on left MACT No. 826/16 Rakesh Vs. Mohd Naushad & Ors. Page No. 8 of 14 leg with distal compound grade II fracture.
It is deposed by him (PW1) that due to the said accident, he himself and his family members have suffered great mental pain, agony, love and affection, loss of income, loss of social activities etc.

So,
considering all these facts, this Tribunal is awarding the award as under:
Medical bills 11.
The petitioner has not placed on record any medical bills being incurred by him on his treatment.
But seeing the nature of injuries being suffered by him.
An amount of Rs.10,000/ is granted to him towards medical expenses.
Loss of Income 12.
The petitioner is claiming that he was doing private job and was earning Rs.15,000/ p.m.
But no specific evidence has come on record to prove the fact of income of the petitioner.
Even otherwise there is no concrete evidence which suggest to this tribunal that there was the fixed income of the petitioner.

Ld Counsel for the petitioner has fairly admitted that petitioner is not having any Rakesh Kumar vs Md Naushad on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24388734/
7 substantial evidence to prove his fixed income.
So in the absence of any documentary proof with regard to income of the petitioner, his income is being assessed as per matriculation of Minimum Wages in Delhi.

At the time of accident the Minimum wages of unskilled labour was Rs. 9,724/
p.m.
Keeping in view the nature of injuries ( fracture of both bones on left leg with distal compound grade II fracture ) received by him and he remained admitted wef 30.12.2016 to 11.01.2017.
It might have taken 5 to 6 months in healing of the injuries.
The petitioner is also granted a sum of

Rs.
58,344/ (Rs.9,724 x6) i.e. equal to six months minimum wages of unskilled labour towards loss of earnings during the period of his treatment.

Pain and Suffering:
14.

The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which he got medical treatment and he was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which he or she faces cannot be considered.

The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination,
such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.

To compensate petitioner under this head, a sum of Rs. 70,000/
is awarded to him.

Mental and physical shock:
15.
As per the petitioner was doing the private job , but due to this mis happening with him his expectations got completely shattered which cannot be compensated in monetary terms.

However,
to console him to an extent, a sum of Rs.25,000/ is awarded to petitioner under this head.

16.

HR55X0981 being driven by respondent no.1 and petitioner suffered injuries in that accident and petitioner is entitled for compensation.

The only submission of Ld Counsel for insurance company is that the Insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It is submitted that the driving license possessed by R.1, at the time of accident, was found fake.
In this regard Respondent No.3 has examined R3W1 ASI Joginder, IO of the case.
He has deposed that during investigation he has found that Driving License No. 9789/2006 dt 12.09.2006 was found being issued in the name of Pinaki Ranjan Mehto.
He has deposed that traffic challan U/S 3/181 M.V Ac was issued against the driver and main challan U/S 5/180, 39/193 M.V Act was issued to owner of offending Car vide DAR Ex R3W1/A.
I have also perused the record annexed with the DAR.
As per verification report received from District Transport Officer, Jamshedpur.
The D/L No.4789/2006 has not been issued to R.1( Mohd Naushad) but the same was issued in the name of one Pinaki Ranjan Mehto .
The evidence adduced on record proves a fact that R.1 was not having a valid driving license at the time of accident.
So this Tribunal has come to the conclusion that R.1 was driving the offending vehicle in contravention of insurance policy.

21. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondents by holding that petitioner is entitled for compensation from respondent no.3, who in turn has a right to recover the same from respondents no.1 and 2 jointly and severally after making payment to the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
He was MACT No. 826/16 Rakesh Vs. Mohd Naushad & Ors.
9. PW 1 has been duly cross examined on behalf of respondent No.3.
The testimony of the PW1 with respect to negligent driving by R.1 could not be impeached.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
The evidence which has come on the file can be considered and becomes more relevant when there is no specific evidence led by other side in rebuttal.
Even otherwise strict rule that negligence is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt is not to be proved in MACT proceedings.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the file only can be considered.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that petitioner was at fault.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which he or she faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination,
such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
So this Tribunal has come to the conclusion that R.1 was driving the offending vehicle in contravention of insurance policy.

of awarded amount be disbursed to the petitioner by way of transferring the same in his saving bank account where from the petitioner would be allowed to withdraw the same through withdrawal slip only and by no other mode/modes i.e. ATM/debit card/credit card/letter/NEFT/RTGS etc.
The Bank Manager, as mentioned in column no.24 of FormV of the petitioner's bank, is directed to convert the 80% of the award amount alongwith interest into two FDRs for two years commencing from one year to two year in the said MACT BANK ACCOUNT of petitioner and after receiving the amount credited in his MACAD ACCOUNT ( Motor Accident Claim Annuity deposit ) The petitioner would be allowed to withdraw the amount only by way of withdrawal slip as stated herein below.

(i) The fixed deposit be renewed automatically till the period prescribed by the Court.
( ii) The interest on the fixed deposit be paid monthly.
(iii) The monthly interest be credited automatically in the saving account of the claimant.
(iv) Original fixed deposit receipt be retained by the bank in safe custody.
However, the original passbook shall be given to the claimant along with the photocopy of the FDR.

826/16 Rakesh Vs. Mohd Naushad & Ors.

(viii) No loan, advance or withdrawal or premature encashment shall be allowed on the fixed deposit without permission of the Court.
25. Respondent no.3 is directed to deposit entire amount of compensation with this tribunal, within 30 days from today, with advance notice to petitioner.
